title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1RC0RF_1LA0LD_0LE0RA_0RB1LD_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1RC0RF_1LA0LD_0LE0RA_0RB1LD_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. Almost the whole tape is 1 0 1 0 …; one or two extra 1s sit inside it and cut it into pieces of nearly equal length, e.g. 890 and 887 copies of 10, or 665, 662 and 441.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 107 steps; the C simulator shows none in 109. How the markers move is not yet understood.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,559 cells have been visited and 1,781 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Tape shape
claims.text: At the side switches near 109 steps the tape is (10)^n with one or two marker 1s: at the right end 1 (10)^1776 (step 991,840,977), 1 (10)^890 1 (10)^888 (step 998,967,199), 1 (10)^665 1 (10)^662 1 (10)^441 (step 985,702,735); at the left end 0 10 0 (10)^1774 0 0 1 (step 991,844,534), 0 (10)^890 1 (10)^887 1 (step 998,960,084).

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.336). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.335).

claims.title: Growth like t<sup>1/3</sup>
claims.text: After step 5·10<sup>8</sup>: 306 side switches, 1,635,180 steps apart on average (≈ 0.129·w<sup>2</sup>, w = 3558), about 2.4 cells of width per switch; fitted width exponent 0.337 after step 10<sup>7</sup>.

claims.title: How it could halt
claims.text: The halting transition is F reading 1. F is entered only from B reading 1 (moving right). So a halt is exactly B>1 1: B on a 1 with a 1 to its right, two adjacent 1s, which the alternating stretch only has next to a marker.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The stretch keeps its alternating shape in every case printed; how the markers move, and why B never reads a 1 next to a 1, are open.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape is an alternating stretch with one or two marker 1s in it that cut it into nearly equal pieces; the markers are rearranged on every trip across the tape, which costs about the width squared, for a few cells of growth: the width grows like the cube root of the time.

facts.text: Width of the tape at its last extension before step 10<sup>9</sup>.
Side switches in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps.

sections.heading: An alternating stretch cut by markers
html: The tape at the last side switches (head at the end shown first):
The marker 1s cut the stretch into pieces of nearly equal length (halves, then thirds), then the pieces are merged back. A halt needs B on two adjacent 1s.

sections.heading: Why the width grows like t<sup>1/3</sup>
html: The head goes back and forth across the whole tape. After step 5·108 there are 306 side switches (extensions of the tape on the other side from the last one), on average 1,635,180 steps apart, which is about 0.129·w2 for the final width w = 3558; each adds about 2.4 cells to the width. A constant gain per w2 steps gives w3 ~ t. The fitted exponent of the width after step 107 is 0.337.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.336). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.335).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,559 cells (1,271 left of the start, 1,624 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: The tape is an alternating stretch 1 0 1 0 … with one or two extra 1s (markers) in it; the markers move so that the stretch is cut in halves, thirds and back to one piece. Width ~ t^(1/3).
